model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, KE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) shown as separate line series. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic (base-10) scale, with major tick labels at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\), spanning roughly from the low tens to beyond one thousand. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, with labeled ticks from 40% up to 65% in 5% increments. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, decreasing from about 39% at the leftmost x-value to about 31% at the rightmost x-value, with intermediate points near ~36% and ~34%. The FT series is a blue solid line with right-pointing triangle markers, declining from about 41% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 33% at the largest, with intermediate values around ~37% and ~35%. The KE series is a red solid line with left-pointing triangle markers, dropping from roughly 44% at the leftmost x-value to roughly 34% at the rightmost, passing through points near ~39% and ~35%. The MEND series is a brown solid line with down-pointing triangle markers, decreasing from about 46–47% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 39–40% at the largest, with intermediate points around ~44% and ~41%. The MEMIT series is a purple solid line with pentagon-like markers, starting near ~46% and remaining close to ~45% at the next x-position before falling to around ~41% and ending near ~37–38%. The ROME series is a green solid line with square markers, decreasing from about 55% at the leftmost x-value to about 47% at the rightmost, with intermediate values around ~53% and ~50%.
